claims.text: ECG for everyone, looking for arrhythmia, conduction problems, hypertrophy, pre-excitation, long QT or Brugada pattern.
claims.quote: ECG is done for all patients. The ECG may reveal arrhythmia, a conduction abnormality, ventricular hypertrophy, pre-excitation, QT prolongation, Brugada syndrome

claims.text: Pulse oximetry during or right after an episode.
claims.quote: Pulse oximetry should be done during or immediately after an episode to identify hypoxemia

claims.text: Labs only as suspected; a pregnancy test in any female of childbearing age, and hematocrit if anemia is suspected.
claims.quote: Laboratory tests are done based on clinical suspicion; reflexively obtained laboratory panels are of little use. However, all females of childbearing age should have a pregnancy test. Hematocrit is measured if anemia is suspected.

claims.text: Echocardiography for unexplained or exercise-induced syncope or a murmur.
claims.quote: Echocardiography (either point-of-care ultrasound [POCUS] or a traditional echocardiogram) is indicated for patients with clinically unexplained syncope, exercise-induced syncope, cardiac murmurs, or suspected intracardiac tumors

claims.text: Sometimes tilt table testing; brain imaging is rarely needed.
claims.quote: Sometimes tilt table testing Blood tests only if clinically indicated Central nervous system imaging rarely indicated
